results.title: Trump’s Iran pressure campaign faces risk of military escalation, analysts say
results.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sought to reassure investors on Thursday that a return to large-scale fighting with Iran was unlikely, even as the Trump administration steps up its economic pressure on Tehran. Bessent said the administration’s decision to pursue maximum economic pressure indicated that an immediate resumption of full-scale military action was unlikely. “If we are doing the maximum economic pressure, then that means that likely there will not be a large-scale kinetic restart,” Bessent told CNBC, while adding that the situation could change. President Donald Trump announced what he called an “economic D-Day” against Iran, warning of unprecedented economic warfare and isolation. He said the measures were aimed at weakening Iran’s economy and its ability to project power abroad. However, analysts said the strategy could create a difficult situation for Washington. Iran is facing shortages, inflation and growing economic pressure, but the administration’s reluctance to resume military action could also encourage Tehran to test US resolve. Dennis B. Ross, a former US Middle East negotiator, said Iranian leaders could interpret Washington’s position as a sign that Trump does not want to escalate militarily, potentially creating an incentive for Iran to respond with military pressure. The US has already imposed extensive sanctions on Iran, while a naval blockade and previous military strikes have added to the pressure on the Iranian economy. The administration faces another challenge in targeting Iran’s economic lifelines, particularly China, which remains the main buyer of Iranian oil. Analysts said further pressure on China could risk tensions between Washington and Beijing. Edward Fishman, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, said the main remaining step in increasing economic pressure on Iran would be to target its trading partners, particularly China. He expressed doubt that Trump would be willing to risk an economic confrontation with Beijing. Iran’s response to the growing economic pressure remains uncertain. Analysts said Tehran could seek to increase military pressure on the United States or its Gulf allies, potentially creating further risks for the Trump administration. Bessent said the Treasury Department would hold a news conference on Monday regarding the new measures targeting Iran.
